title: A flaw was found in ModemManager.
desc: A flaw was found in ModemManager. When parsing a Cell Broadcast Message, some 3GPP data-coding-scheme values (8-bit and reserved character sets) are not handled. The process hits a reachable assertion and aborts. An attacker who can deliver a crafted Cell Broadcast PDU over the radio network, or via a modem AT channel, can cause ModemManager to exit. Repeated aborts can exhaust systemd's default start limit and leave the service failed.

title: The Easy Social Share Buttons for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the 'design' parameter in all versions up to, and including…
desc: The Easy Social Share Buttons for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the 'design' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 11.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute if they can successfully trick a user into performing an action such as clicking on a link. title: When DNS over HTTPS is enabled and a caching HTTP reverse proxy is used in front of DNSdist, it is possible to pollute the cache of the HTTP reverse proxy by sending DNS over…

title: A code injection vulnerability exists in Epiphany when the user invokes form autofill from the context menu on a page containing a malicious HTML form.
desc:
A code injection vulnerability exists in Epiphany when the user invokes form autofill from the context menu on a page containing a malicious HTML form.

In embed/web-process-extension/resources/js/ephy_autofill.js, getSelector() builds a CSS selector by directly interpolating an element's id attribute:

    path.unshift(`#${el.id}`);

When the user selects an autofill entry, the browser process in embed/ephy-web-view.c previously constructed JavaScript using sprintf with the selector embedded in single quotes:

    EphyAutofill.fill(PAGE_ID, 'SELECTOR', FILL_CHOICE);

Because SELECTOR comes from attacker-controlled page content and is not escaped, a crafted id such as a'); PAYLOAD; var _=(' breaks out of the string literal and executes arbitrary JavaScript when the script is evaluated.

The injected code runs in Epiphany's private autofill script world, which hosts EphyAutofill credential APIs and password manager save/request handlers. The reporter demonstrated a proof of concept that injects credentials into another domain and uses Ephy.permissionsManager to enumerate domains with special permissions. Full exfiltration of all saved passwords was not demonstrated but may be possible given the privileges of this context.

Exploitation requires the victim to visit a malicious page, right-click on a form field, and choose an Autofill context menu item. This is a deliberate user action but does not require installing software or entering credentials manually.

Affected versions: Epiphany >= 47.beta.
Fixed upstream in epiphany 50.6 and 49.9 via merge request !2147, which replaces sprintf-based script evaluation with a WebKit user message and jsc_value_object_invoke_method() passing the selector as a typed string argument.
Upstream report: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/epiphany/-/issues/2921

title: A path traversal (ZIP slip) vulnerability exists in Epiphany when installing WebExtension packages from .xpi files.
desc:
A path traversal (ZIP slip) vulnerability exists in Epiphany when installing WebExtension packages from .xpi files.

In src/webextension/ephy-web-extension-manager.c, the decompress_xpi_thread() function extracts XPI archives (ZIP format) to disk using libarchive. For each archive entry, the output path is built by concatenating the intended extraction directory with the raw pathname from the archive:

    full_path = g_build_filename(path, archive_entry_pathname(entry), NULL);
    archive_entry_set_pathname(entry, full_path);
    ret = archive_write_header(ext, entry);

The libarchive extraction options did not include ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_NODOTDOT or ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_SYMLINKS. As a result, archive entries containing parent-directory traversal sequences (for example "../../../../../.bashrc") are written outside the intended web_extensions extraction directory.

A malicious .xpi file can therefore overwrite arbitrary files writable by the user running Epiphany, such as ~/.bashrc, ~/.config/autostart/*.desktop, or ~/.ssh/authorized_keys. This can lead to persistent code execution on subsequent shell startup or GNOME login.

Exploitation requires the victim to install or open a crafted .xpi file. The reporter notes that opening an XPI can trigger extraction even when the WebExtensions feature is not enabled by default.

Affected versions: Epiphany >= 47.rc.
Fixed upstream in epiphany 50.6 and 49.9 via merge request !2143, which adds ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_NODOTDOT and ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_SYMLINKS to archive_write_disk_set_options().
Upstream report: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/epiphany/-/issues/2922

title: MONEO ERP exposes the Ping method of its _slave JSON-RPC service over WebSocket as @rpc.openpublic, so it can be called without a valid session.
desc: MONEO ERP exposes the Ping method of its _slave JSON-RPC service over WebSocket as @rpc.openpublic, so it can be called without a valid session. The method's only guard compares the calling application name with "_login", but that value is taken from the client-controlled params.appname field of the request. When the check passes, Ping stores an attacker-chosen session ID, user number and company in the server session store, and subsequent session validation accepts that session. An unauthenticated remote attacker can therefore create a valid session as any user, including administrators, in any company (tenant) hosted on the server and invoke authenticated RPC methods with that user's privileges, gaining read and write access to that company's data.

title: A flaw was found in Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security (ACS).
desc: A flaw was found in Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security (ACS). An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit a vulnerability in the login interface's OAuth callback endpoint by crafting a malicious URL. This URL, containing unvalidated `error` and `error_uri` parameters, allows the attacker to display arbitrary error messages, leading to content spoofing. Furthermore, the attacker can redirect victims to malicious domains, effectively performing an open redirect under the guise of the trusted application's user interface.

title: A flaw was found in CRI-O.
desc: A flaw was found in CRI-O. An attacker with access to the kubelet or CRI-O socket can exploit a path traversal vulnerability in the checkpoint restore functionality. This allows the attacker to delete arbitrary files and directories on the host filesystem during a checkpoint restore operation. The vulnerability arises because the system processes entries from checkpoint archive metadata without validating that the files are confined to the container's root directory.

Attackers can send a crafted email with a text/enriched part so that script injected into the HTML editor runs in the victim's session when the victim replies to, forwards, or edits the message.

An authenticated user of the SQL address book can supply other users' group and contact identifiers to add contacts to or remove them from other users' contact groups, or to add other users' contacts to their own groups.

desc: Pillow through 13.1.0 contains an integer overflow in the ImageMath integer divide and modulo operators (DIV_I and MOD_I in src/_imagingmath.c), which guard only against a zero divisor, so dividing INT32_MIN by -1 raises a hardware divide exception. Attackers can supply a crafted TIFF that decodes to a mode I image containing INT32_MIN, crashing applications that run an ImageMath divide or modulo with a -1 operand on it.

title: Sparkle 2.2.0 before 2.9.6 contains a link following vulnerability in -submitInstallerAtPath: in SUInstallerLauncher.m that builds a root updater's launcher cache path inside the…
desc: Sparkle 2.2.0 before 2.9.6 contains a link following vulnerability in -submitInstallerAtPath: in SUInstallerLauncher.m that builds a root updater's launcher cache path inside the console user's home directory and then deletes and creates items there without rejecting symbolic links. A local console user can pre-create that path as a symlink while a CLI tool or daemon updates a bundle as root, making root delete old files in a directory of the attacker's choosing and create a directory there that is chowned to the attacker, leading to privilege escalation.

title: Sparkle before 2.9.6 contains a time-of-check time-of-use race condition in the installer's SPUInstallationData handling in AppInstaller.m, which validates the symlink-resolved…
desc: Sparkle before 2.9.6 contains a time-of-check time-of-use race condition in the installer's SPUInstallationData handling in AppInstaller.m, which validates the symlink-resolved download URL but performs the privileged move on the unresolved URL and checks the file type only afterwards. A local user can swap an intermediate directory of the download path for a symlink between the check and the move, causing a root installer to rename a file out of a protected location and leading to privilege escalation when the installer runs in the system domain.

title: PDFio before 1.6.5 contains an integer underflow in _pdfioCryptoAESDecrypt() in pdfio-aes.c, which strips PKCS#7 padding before any AES block has been decrypted when an…
desc: PDFio before 1.6.5 contains an integer underflow in _pdfioCryptoAESDecrypt() in pdfio-aes.c, which strips PKCS#7 padding before any AES block has been decrypted when an AES-encrypted string or binary value holds only its 16-byte IV. Attackers can supply a crafted AES-encrypted PDF that, when opened with pdfioFileOpen(), makes the decrypted length underflow so that _pdfioValueDecrypt() reads and writes out of bounds, crashing the application or corrupting heap memory.

title: FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in pcx_encode_frame() in libavcodec/pcxenc.c that rounds each row up to an even number of bytes and run-length…

title: Flowintel contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in its HedgeDoc case-notes integration.
desc:
Flowintel contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in its HedgeDoc case-notes integration. When a user with editor or administrator privileges associates a HedgeDoc URL with a case, the application later issues a server-side HTTP GET request to that URL to retrieve note content. Before the fix, the stored URL was used directly without validation of its scheme, host, port, path, or userinfo, and the HTTP client followed redirects by default with no connect or read timeouts.

An authenticated attacker could therefore cause the Flowintel server to issue requests to arbitrary internal or external endpoints (for example, cloud instance-metadata services, internal management interfaces, or other intranet hosts) and receive the response body, or follow a redirect chain to an unintended destination. The absence of timeouts also permitted resource-exhaustion against the server's outbound connection pool.

Preconditions:
- An authenticated account with editor or administrator role on the target case.
- The HedgeDoc integration feature is enabled (no explicit configuration gate existed before the fix).

Impact:
- Disclosure of sensitive data served by internal or cloud-metadata endpoints.
- Potential denial of service through unbounded outbound requests.

Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

title: Lookyloo is a web-based malware analysis and sandboxing platform.
desc: Lookyloo is a web-based malware analysis and sandboxing platform. The pull-from-remote-instance feature allows a user to request a previously captured sample from another Lookyloo instance by specifying the target instance's URL and a capture UUID. Prior to the fix, the only restriction on the target URL was a check that the hostname, if it was a literal IP address, was not in a private range. Hostnames that resolved to private or internal addresses were not blocked, and no authentication or allowlist was enforced for anonymous users. This allowed any unauthenticated user to direct the Lookyloo server to issue HTTP requests (HEAD to the root path and GET to /json/<uuid>/status, followed by a capture download) to arbitrary internal or external hosts, effectively enabling a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attack. An attacker could use this to probe internal network topology, access captures stored on internal Lookyloo instances, or leverage the server as a proxy to reach otherwise unreachable services. The vulnerability is in the website/web/__init__.py module, specifically the __get_remote_capture function and the associated pull endpoint. The security impact is unauthorized disclosure of capture data and internal service information from Lookyloo instances that are not intended to be publicly accessible.

The connectURL field of a VirtualMachineInstanceMigration object is not validated at admission, and the privileged synchronization-controller dials the attacker-specified URL. Connection and DNS errors from the dial are exposed in a condition readable in the tenant's namespace. A user with the kubevirt.io:migrate role (a role designed for tenant delegation) can use this behavior as a blind network-reconnaissance oracle to determine the existence and connectivity of internal hosts and ports from the controller's network vantage, including services isolated from the tenant by network policy. TLS certificate pinning prevents session completion with non-KubeVirt hosts, limiting the impact to information disclosure of internal network topology; no data content, integrity, or availability impact is possible.

title: The Simple Membership plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.0 The vulnerability exists because the…
desc: The Simple Membership plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.0 The vulnerability exists because the `bulk_operation_menu()` function accepts the `swpm_bulk_change_level_to` parameter from `$_REQUEST` with only `sanitize_text_field()` applied, and passes it to `SwpmMemberUtils::update_membership_level_and_role()` without the `id != 1` allowlist exclusion that every other level-selection path in the plugin enforces — leaving membership level 1, which the installer maps to the WordPress `administrator` role on every fresh install, freely selectable as a bulk-change target. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access and above to elevate their own WordPress account to the full Administrator role, gaining complete site control including plugin installation, user creation, and all other administrator capabilities. Exploitation requires that an administrator has first lowered the plugin's "Admin Dashboard Access Permission" setting from its default of `manage_options` to a lesser capability such as `edit_posts` (Contributor), `edit_published_posts` (Author), or `edit_pages` (Editor), which is a non-default granted-access configuration; the bulk screen's nonce protection (`swpm_bulk_change_level_nonce_action`) does not mitigate the issue because the nonce is emitted on the same page the delegated lower-role user can already reach. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete administrator role.

title: The Simple Membership plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.0 This is due to the `SwpmLevelForm::role()` function…

Exploitation requires that the site owner has lowered the plugin's "Admin Dashboard Access Permission" setting from its default `manage_options` capability to a lesser capability such as `edit_posts`, `edit_published_posts`, or `edit_pages`, which grants lower-privileged users access to the SWPM admin dashboard where the vulnerable level-creation form resides. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete administrator role.

title: An **uncontrolled memory allocation** flaw has been found in the smbd_smb2_ioctl_pipe_write_done() function in source3/smbd/smb2_ioctl_named_pipe.c of the SMB2 named-pipe ioctl…
desc: An **uncontrolled memory allocation** flaw has been found in the smbd_smb2_ioctl_pipe_write_done() function in source3/smbd/smb2_ioctl_named_pipe.c of the SMB2 named-pipe ioctl handling in the **Samba** package. The file server reserves memory for a named-pipe response using a size chosen by the client. It does not keep that size within the maximum the client and the server have already agreed. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can open a named pipe can request a very large response. The file server reserves that memory before it reads the pipe and holds it until the request ends. Repeating this on more connections can exhaust memory and keep the file service unavailable while those requests continue.

desc: A flaw was found in Flatpak’s flatpak-portal. When a sandboxed application invokes Spawn() and maps two different file descriptors to the same handle, dup2() can fail. Affected Flatpak versions do not handle that failure, so a file descriptor that was open inside flatpak-portal (commonly the unfiltered D-Bus session bus) can be passed into the subsandbox. A malicious or compromised Flatpak app with no special privileges can use this to escape the sandbox.

title: A flaw was found in Flatpak’s flatpak-system-helper.
desc: A flaw was found in Flatpak’s flatpak-system-helper. Affected Flatpak versions can still report success without clearing setuid/setgid bits, leaving a setuid-root executable under /var/lib/flatpak. A local attacker who can install or update such content system-wide, or who can already execute code as a local user in cooperation with that content, can escalate privileges to root.

title: A **Type Confusion** has been found in the dns_to_dnsp_convert() function in dnsdata.c of the DNS server RPC module in the **Samba** package.
desc: A **Type Confusion** has been found in the dns_to_dnsp_convert() function in dnsdata.c of the DNS server RPC module in the **Samba** package. The function copies an HINFO record from the management request into the stored DNS record without converting the request name into the two strings the stored record uses. A low-privileged network attacker or user in the DnsAdmins group adds an HINFO record through the DNS management interface. The directory process that handles the add also serves the directory's other remote calls. That process exits, which disconnects the clients that were using it, and the directory service starts a replacement process. Another add of the same kind crashes the process that accepts it, and each further crash waits longer before that process is replaced, so repeating the add keeps the directory remote-call service from staying available.

The function uses the sort value from the search result with no check that the result still contains that attribute. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can search the directory sends a Virtual List View search by value, sorted on an attribute the matching entries do not have. The LDAP worker that handles the search exits, which disconnects the directory clients that were using that worker, and the directory service starts a replacement worker. Another search of the same kind crashes the worker that accepts it, and each further crash waits longer before that worker is replaced, so repeating the search keeps the LDAP service from staying available. The same crash follows a search sorted on an attribute the attacker is not allowed to read. The directory removes that attribute from the result, and the comparison uses the missing value.

title: The W3 Total Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized File Deletion in all versions up to, and including, 2.11.0 via the `ajax_revert()` AJAX handler.
desc: The W3 Total Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized File Deletion in all versions up to, and including, 2.11.0 via the `ajax_revert()` AJAX handler. The vulnerability exists because the `remove_optimizations()` function reads attacker-controlled values from the unprotected `w3tc_imageservice` post meta key — which carries no underscore prefix and no registered authorization callback, making it writable by any user with `edit_post` capability via WordPress's built-in custom-fields AJAX endpoint — and passes those values directly to `wp_delete_attachment()` with no check that the referenced ID is a child of the caller's own post, is an actual attachment, or that the caller holds `delete_post` capability on it. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Author-level access or above to permanently delete any WordPress attachment in the media library, including media files owned by other users along with their associated files on disk, regardless of ownership — a capability not available through the normal WordPress interface. The revert nonce is exposed via `wp_localize_script` on `/wp-admin/upload.php` to any user with `upload_files` capability, ensuring the nonce check that is present does not serve as a meaningful barrier to Author-level exploitation.

desc: The Product Options and Price Calculation Formulas for WooCommerce – Uni CPO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'price_disabled_msg' setting in versions up to, and including, 4.9.69 The uni_cpo_save_settings_data() AJAX handler applies html_entity_decode() to the output of uni_cpo_sanitize_text(), which itself already runs html_entity_decode() before wp_kses(); this double decode allows a double-entity-encoded tag to pass wp_kses as inert text and then be re-materialised as live HTML before being stored in the _cpo_price_disabled_msg post meta and later echoed via do_shortcode() on the single-product page without further escaping. Exploitation requires a user-registration form with manual approval enabled and a user confirmation email that includes the {all_fields} merge tag (the default template). title: The Schema & Structured Data for WP & AMP plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in versions up to, and including, 1.68.
desc: The Schema & Structured Data for WP & AMP plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in versions up to, and including, 1.68. This is due to deserialization of untrusted input via the admin export (saswp_export_all_settings_and_schema) which calls unrestricted unserialize() on every raw post meta value, combined with saswp_review_form_process_data() which stores unauthenticated-visitor-supplied reviewer-name data through update_post_meta — the plugin sanitizes with sanitize_text_field(), which does not recognise PHP serialization syntax or the NUL property-name delimiters, and WordPress's maybe_serialize/is_serialized has no case for the legacy PHP 'C' custom-serialization token (ArrayObject), so the payload is persisted byte-for-byte and never wrapped in a protective extra serialize layer. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject a PHP Object into the processing of the plugin. No known POP chain is present in the vulnerable plugin itself, but if a suitable chain exists via an additional plugin or theme installed on the blog, it could be used to delete arbitrary files, or achieve other impacts. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

title: A path traversal vulnerability in Medusa’s product import functionality, specifically in the handling of the 'file_key' parameter of the '/admin/products/imports' endpoint.
desc: A path traversal vulnerability in Medusa’s product import functionality, specifically in the handling of the 'file_key' parameter of the '/admin/products/imports' endpoint. The lack of proper validation allows an authenticated remote attacker with administrative access to reference system files outside the intended import directory. When attempting to process these files as CSV files, the application may partially reveal their contents through parsing or validation error messages. Additionally, cleanup routines operate on paths controlled by the attacker, which could allow the deletion of files accessible to the application process and affect system availability.

title: The Smaily Connect plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in versions up to, and including, 3.24.0 This is due to the smaily_get_edit_user_id()…
desc: The Smaily Connect plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in versions up to, and including, 3.24.0 This is due to the smaily_get_edit_user_id() function reading an attacker-controlled $_GET['user_id'] parameter without performing any ownership or capability check, and then feeding that id into smaily_get_userdata() (which calls get_user_meta()) when rendering the WooCommerce My Account 'edit-account' form via the smaily_print_user_frontend_fields() handler on the woocommerce_edit_account_form action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to read other users' personally identifiable profile data (phone number, date of birth, and gender — including administrators') by appending ?user_id=<target> to the account-details URL.

title: GNU m4 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in reload_frozen_state() in src/freeze.c.
desc:
GNU m4 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in reload_frozen_state() in src/freeze.c. When processing a malicious frozen-state file via the -R option, an attacker can trigger an oversized allocation request that crashes the program, causing denial of service.


This issue was fixed in commit 69aef802fb25ab600d37210f44e5128633cbc432.

title: A Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in the eventbus execution in Google Cloud Application Integration versions prior to 2026-09-22 on Google Cloud Platform allows…
desc:
A Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in the eventbus execution in Google Cloud Application Integration versions prior to 2026-09-22 on Google Cloud Platform allows an authenticated attacker to achieve remote code execution using a crafted serialized Java object.


This vulnerability was patched on 22 September 2026, and no customer action is needed.

title: The Sneeit Framework plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in versions up to, and including, 8.7 via the 'callback' parameter of the…
desc: The Sneeit Framework plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in versions up to, and including, 8.7 via the 'callback' parameter of the sneeit_compact_menu_mega_content AJAX action. The handler sneeit_compact_menu_mega_content_callback() is registered on the wp_ajax_nopriv_ hook and passes the attacker-supplied 'callback' value directly into call_user_func() after only a function_exists() check, with the single argument also attacker-controlled via a JSON-decoded 'args' parameter. There is no authentication, no capability check, no nonce, and no allow-list of callable functions. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary existing PHP/WordPress functions with controlled arguments.
